specs.anchorText: Get the encoder right and the same generator suddenly obeys instructions it used to ignore.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a cheerful little workshop where a friendly robot reads a handwritten note that says only a tiny heart-and-corgi doodle, and hands it across a counter to a paintbrush-wielding robot artist who is happily painting a picture of a corgi on an easel. Between them a glowing arrow turns the words into a small floating vector orb that the artist catches. The note-reader robot points (does not paint); the artist paints (does not read). Soft pastel background, clean white space, gentle and inclusive mood, comic-strip energy like XKCD meets Kurzgesagt. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on the single idea of translating a sentence into something a painter can use.
specs.alt: A note-reading robot hands a glowing vector orb to a painting robot, who turns it into a corgi on an easel, showing that a frozen text encoder translates the prompt while a separate generator does the actual drawing.
specs.caption: Before anything can be drawn, the sentence has to be translated into something a painter can use; the reader and the painter are two different machines with two different jobs.

specs.anchorText: The mnemonic: CLIP reads the menu, T5 reads the sentence.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: two friendly cartoon readers sitting side by side at a cozy cafe table. On the left, a robot squints at a menu and has only loose floating word-bubbles of disconnected items (an apple shape, a pear shape, a number) drifting around its head in no order. On the right, a calmer scholarly robot wearing small reading glasses reads a full sentence on a scroll, and above its head the same items are neatly arranged in correct order with little linking ribbons showing which adjective binds to which object. Warm soft background, generous margins, gentle humor, inclusive and approachable, XKCD-inspired. No text or lettering in the image. Focus on the contrast between a bag of loose concepts and a well-ordered sentence.
specs.alt: A robot reading a menu sees loose unordered concept bubbles while a robot reading a full sentence sees the same concepts neatly ordered and linked, illustrating that CLIP captures a bag of concepts while a T5 language encoder preserves grammar, counts, and word binding.
specs.caption: One encoder counts the words and shrugs at the grammar; the other reads the whole sentence, which is exactly why word order and counting survive the trip into the model.

specs.anchorText: The architecture is a pipeline, and Figure 34.2.1 is the map.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly three-station factory line shown as three connected little buildings. Station one is a tiny press labeled by an icon that shrinks a big picture down into a small compact cube on a conveyor belt. Station two is a busy workshop where a robot painter works only on the small cube, repeatedly cleaning fog off it while a separate robot whispers into its ear through an ear-trumpet (the text whisper). Station three is a press that blows the small finished cube back up into a full-size framed picture. A conveyor belt connects all three left to right. Warm pastel palette, clean white background, generous margins, gentle and approachable, comic-strip style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep it simple: three stations, one belt, one small cube traveling through.
specs.alt: A three-station cartoon factory: a press shrinks an image into a small cube, a workshop robot repeatedly cleans the small cube while another robot whispers text into its ear, and a final press enlarges the finished cube back into a full picture, depicting the VAE encoder, the denoising U-Net with cross-attention, and the VAE decoder.
specs.caption: Stable Diffusion is three machines in a row: one shrinks the world, one paints inside the shrunken world while a sentence whispers in its ear, and one blows the result back up to scale.

specs.anchorText: they all sit at the same coordinates in Table 34.3.1
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly family of sibling robots standing together at an awkward reunion, all clearly built from the same body design but each adjusting three big control dials on its chest. The dials are labeled by tiny icons only: one dial shows a speech bubble (the encoder), one shows a paintbrush (the generator), one shows a polish-sparkle (the data and finishing). Each sibling has its dials set to slightly different positions, and one sibling stands proudly holding a small framed picture that looks more polished than the others. Warm pastel background, clean white space, gentle group-photo humor, inclusive and diverse robot designs, XKCD-inspired. No text or lettering in the image. Focus on identical bodies with differently set dials.
specs.alt: A family of identical sibling robots at a reunion, each turning three chest dials marked with a speech bubble, a paintbrush, and a polish sparkle to different settings, showing that every text-to-image system is the same three-station template with the encoder, generator, and data-and-finishing knobs turned differently.
specs.caption: The big-name models are not rivals so much as the same recipe arguing over which encoder to hire and how much to retouch the photos afterward.

specs.anchorText: The mnemonic for the two paths: diffusion polishes the whole canvas at once; tokens write it like a sentence.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a split scene comparing two friendly robots making the same picture two ways. On the left, a robot stands before a single big canvas and polishes the entire surface at once with a wide squeegee, a foggy image becoming clear everywhere simultaneously. On the right, a robot writes the same picture as a left-to-right row of small tile-stamps on a strip, like writing a sentence, placing one little patch-tile after another in reading order. Warm pastel background, clean white space, generous margins, gentle humor, inclusive, comic-strip style like XKCD. No text or lettering in the image. Focus on whole-canvas-at-once versus one-tile-at-a-time.
specs.alt: Two robots create the same image differently: one polishes an entire foggy canvas clear all at once, the other lays down small patch tiles left to right like writing a sentence, contrasting diffusion's parallel-in-space refinement with autoregressive token generation that commits one position at a time.
specs.caption: Diffusion and token generation share the same goal and differ only in order: one clears the whole canvas at once, the other writes the picture like a sentence, one patch at a time.

specs.anchorText: Table 34.6.1 lays out the ladder; the rest of the section explains each rung.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly robot standing on a small four-rung ladder that leans against a giant library shelf full of pictures (its existing knowledge). On the heaviest bottom rung the robot is repainting the entire library and looking worried as old pictures smudge; on each higher, lighter rung it carries a smaller and smaller toolkit (a big paint bucket, then a small clip-on adapter patch, then a single tiny glowing word-card), and the library behind it stays crisp and untouched. The robot looks calmer the higher and lighter it goes. Warm pastel background, clean white space, generous margins, gentle humor, inclusive, XKCD-inspired. No text or lettering in the image. Focus on heavier change risking smudged shelves, lighter change leaving the library intact.
specs.alt: A robot on a four-rung ladder against a shelf of existing pictures: on the heaviest rung it repaints the whole shelf and smudges old images, while on lighter rungs it uses ever-smaller tools (a small adapter patch, a single glowing word-card) and the shelf stays intact, illustrating the fine-tuning ladder from full fine-tune to DreamBooth to LoRA to textual inversion and the freeze-more-forget-less principle.
specs.caption: The fine-tuning ladder is one long bargain: the more of the model you freeze, the less of the dictionary you bulldoze while learning a single new word.

specs.anchorText: it is a tradeoff, and pushing it past the sweet spot trades adherence gains for artifacts
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly robot enthusiastically cranking a big dial labeled by a tiny up-arrow icon way past a marked green sweet-spot zone into a red zone. As it cranks too far, the picture on its easel goes from a pleasant balanced painting to an over-saturated, blown-out, neon, crunchy mess, and the robot winces sheepishly. A small gauge nearby shows the needle pinned in the red. Warm pastel background, clean white space, generous margins, gentle self-deprecating humor, inclusive, comic-strip style like XKCD. No text or lettering in the image. Focus on the dial cranked past the safe zone causing an oversaturated, artifacted image.
specs.alt: A robot cranks a guidance dial far past a green sweet-spot zone into the red, and its easel painting turns oversaturated, neon, and crunchy with artifacts, showing that pushing classifier-free guidance scale too high trades prompt adherence for oversaturation and contrast blowout.
specs.caption: Guidance scale is not a quality dial that goes to eleven; crank it past the sweet spot and you trade prompt adherence for oversaturated, artifacted images.
